premise.title: The Road the Map Refused to Admit
premise.logline: During a routine re-survey of Ashen Gate, Leyra finds that a century-sealed boundary is answering to a road the legal map insists does not exist, while a private field mark tied to her mentor suggests someone investigated the anomaly before her.
premise.protagonist_role: Eighteen-year-old junior boundary cartographer preparing for an independent map-seal license in a guild where witnessed geography can become magically binding.
premise.immediate_objective: Establish exactly what Ashen Gate is doing before dusk and decide what she can responsibly report without turning an extraordinary discovery into an unsupported claim.
premise.inciting_event: Leyra's ward-compass and an exterior boundary stone both respond as though a route continues through Ashen Gate, even though the legal map records the passage as sealed.
premise.central_problem: Leyra must separate a genuine change in the boundary from misleading magical residue while pressure from Greyfen and the guild makes both silence and overstatement consequential.
premise.wonder_or_discovery: The sealed arch appears to recognize a line that current maps deny, and an old private survey mark associated with Master Ilyan may be present near the gate without explaining what he knew or why he left it.
premise.stakes: A false reopening claim could make travelers trust an unstable magical road and end Leyra's apprenticeship; ignoring a real boundary change could leave Greyfen relying on a map that no longer describes the world.
constraints: Leyra may survey the exterior markers but may not cross the sealed boundary without authorization.
A private field mark can establish prior presence or survey activity but cannot prove motive, cause or a hidden conspiracy.
One session cannot prove why the road returned, what lies in the Nameless Vale, or whether other sealed roads are changing.
Any durable map claim must distinguish witnessed response from theory.
premise.meaningful_choice_pressure: Before the useful light and ward-response window fades, Leyra must choose how much time to spend trying to reproduce the gate response versus preserving a bounded report and confronting the fact that her mentor may have marked this place before.
premise.mystery_or_forward_question: Why is Ashen Gate answering to a road erased from legal maps, and what did Master Ilyan actually witness here years ago?
premise.local_payoff: The episode must resolve what Leyra can honestly put on record now. It may establish one bounded Ashen Gate anomaly, but must leave cause, wider scope, the Nameless Vale and Master Ilyan's motives unresolved unless evidence explicitly earns more.
persistent_outcomes_possible: forbidden_passage_observed becomes eligible if Leyra produces a dated bounded field record of the gate response
Greyfen gains a concrete but carefully worded reason to monitor the old boundary
Leyra's professional trust with Master Ilyan may shift based on how she handles incomplete evidence
an authorized follow-up survey may become possible without the passage being declared safe or reopened
world_specific_elements: ward-compasses that answer only to witnessed boundary lines
maps whose sealed claims can stabilize real roads and borders
private cartographer field marks that are informative but not legal proof

dimensions.name: PREMISE_MATURITY
dimensions.description: Core conflict should match the target reader's autonomy and conceptual range rather than relying on vocabulary to imply maturity.

dimensions.name: NARRATIVE_COMPLEXITY
dimensions.description: Support layered goals, changing information, reversals, parallel pressures, and earned resolution.

dimensions.name: CONCEPTUAL_COMPLEXITY
dimensions.description: Allow systems, institutions, evidence, ethics, ambiguity, identity, responsibility, and competing explanations at the target level.

dimensions.name: CAUSAL_DEPTH
dimensions.description: Important outcomes should arise from several linked causes, decisions, constraints, and consequences.

dimensions.name: INFERENCE_DEMAND
dimensions.description: Allow meaningful unstated connections and interpretation without making essential causality opaque.

dimensions.name: AGENCY_COMPLEXITY
dimensions.description: The protagonist should make consequential strategic choices among credible alternatives.

dimensions.name: STAKES_CONSEQUENCE_COMPLEXITY
dimensions.description: Stakes may affect reputation, relationships, livelihood, access, identity, institutions, safety, or world state without becoming melodramatic by default.

dimensions.name: SOCIAL_RELATIONSHIP_COMPLEXITY
dimensions.description: Support mixed motives, power differences, trust, conflict, loyalty, negotiation, and changing relationships without flattening people into roles.

dimensions.name: PREDICTABILITY_CHALLENGE
dimensions.description: Avoid obvious one-beat solutions; permit wrong models, reversals, incomplete information, and trade-offs.

dimensions.name: WONDER_DISCOVERY
dimensions.description: Adventure-oriented stories should still offer discovery, exploration, systems, mystery, or experiences larger than routine simulation.

dimensions.name: LANGUAGE_READABILITY
dimensions.description: Use clear, natural language appropriate to an independent adult reader; complexity should come from thought and structure, not unnecessary opacity.

required_story_capabilities: A protagonist with a credible age-appropriate role and independent agency
At least one layered objective, unresolved question, or competing priority
Multi-step causality with consequences that accumulate across the episode
A meaningful change in understanding rather than simple clue collection
A consequential choice, strategic trade-off, or irreversible local action
A local episode payoff that does not prematurely close long-horizon questions
Persistent consequence or reusable world-state value when earned
Adventure-oriented modes should include genuine discovery, exploration, mystery, or systems engagement
reject_signals: A premise made to feel older mainly through harder vocabulary
One obvious attempt solves the central problem without meaningful complication
The protagonist mostly observes while another character resolves the core problem
Exposition or lore substitutes for scene-level causality and choice
Mystery or conflict resolves by coincidence, withheld information, or unearned revelation
Violence, trauma, romance, cynicism, or darkness is added merely to signal maturity
The world could be replaced by a generic setting without materially changing the problem
language_rules: Prefer precise natural language over ornamental density
Domain-specific terminology is allowed when it serves action, reasoning, profession, or world logic and remains understandable in context
Do not use vocabulary difficulty as a substitute for premise or conceptual maturity
Let dialogue, action, evidence, and consequence carry interpretation where practical
Avoid juvenile narration unless the exact character voice or scene intentionally calls for it
safety_rules: Maturity does not require graphic violence, sexual content, trauma, or despair
Tension, danger, loss, rivalry, moral uncertainty, and difficult relationships may appear when relevant and proportionate
Do not force age stereotypes, illness, frailty, parenthood, nostalgia, or romance merely because the reader is older
calibration_notes: Age-18 stories may use adult-scale autonomy, institutions, ethical tension, identity, work/study responsibility, and ambiguous motives without assuming adult life experience.
Do not make the story feel adult merely by adding darker content or denser vocabulary.
Product session length remains separately governed by the cross-age qualification matrix.
Cross-age qualification authority: STANDARD product session is fixed at 1,600–2,500 words for the first controlled 12/18/25/40/60 proof so maturity is isolated from length.

character.name: Leyra
character.archetype: junior boundary cartographer and ward-map apprentice
traits: protective of people who trust maps
character.origin_summary: Leyra grew up in Greyfen watching adults trust boundary maps they could not read. At eighteen she is a junior ward-map apprentice at Vellum Hall, close to earning the right to seal independent surveys.
character.current_role: junior boundary cartographer under independent map-seal review

identity_anchors.statement: Leyra believes a map should never claim more than its maker can honestly witness.
Leyra is drawn to impossible places but refuses to call mystery proof.

core_drives.drive: Earn the right to chart places current maps cannot explain.
Keep border communities from paying the price for elegant but wrong maps.

internal_tensions.side_b: powerful desire to cross into the unknown
internal_tensions.description: Leyra's best discoveries tempt her to move faster than the rules that make those discoveries trustworthy.

immediate_desires: prove that wonder and discipline can coexist in serious cartography
immediate_avoidances: inventing certainty because a discovery feels important
being dismissed as a reckless village-born apprentice

world.era: late guild age in a kingdom whose borders are maintained by enchanted survey networks
world.habitat: forested border marches divided by old roads, warded valleys, ruined watch-lines and map-bound settlements
world.technology_level: ink presses, compasses, chain measures, glass lenses, horse travel and guild archives
world.magic_level: strong but rule-bound cartographic magic: witnessed boundaries can be sealed into maps, wardstones answer only to measured lines, and unverified geography cannot safely be written as fact
world.summary: The Veiled Marches are held together by maps that do more than describe roads and borders: once properly witnessed and sealed, they help stabilize them. Old routes sometimes disappear behind ward-lines, and the guild treats sealed passages as dangerous until independently re-surveyed. The magic rewards observation, corroboration and exact wording; a confident false map can be more dangerous than an incomplete one.
social_context: licensed cartographers carry both practical and magical authority
border villages depend on guild maps but bear the consequences when maps are wrong
crossing a sealed boundary without a survey warrant can end an apprenticeship
senior cartographers may maintain private field marks, but those marks are not legal evidence by themselves
old folktales about roads returning are common and usually dismissed as exaggeration
known_pressures: several outer wardstones have become harder to reconcile with legal maps
spring caravans will soon increase traffic through the border marches
Greyfen wants certainty before moving livestock near the old boundary
the guild fears panic caused by unverified claims about forgotten roads
known_world_facts: Leyra is an eighteen-year-old junior boundary cartographer based at Vellum Hall.
Ashen Gate is legally recorded as sealed and has not been formally reopened.
Greyfen lies beside the eastern ward-line and depends on stable boundary maps.
A legal map-seal requires witnessed survey evidence; private marks and rumors are not enough.
Crossing a sealed boundary without authorization can end an apprenticeship.
Master Ilyan trained Leyra and has never given her a clear account of his earlier Ashen Gate work.
No accepted evidence currently proves why old roads sometimes appear to return.

main_saga_public.title: The Unwritten Border
main_saga_public.goal: Discover why Ashen Gate and other retired boundary lines can begin answering to roads that legal maps say no longer exist.
main_saga_public.stakes: Wrongly restoring a dangerous road could expose border communities to unstable magic, while wrongly suppressing a real route could leave the guild blind to a changing world.
main_saga_public.central_mystery: The old boundary network is changing state according to rules the current guild only partly understands.

eligible_main_saga_milestones.summary: Leyra documents a repeatable visible or magical response showing that Ashen Gate currently answers to a path the legal map marks as sealed.
eligible_main_saga_milestones.state_condition: A dated field record establishes one bounded anomaly at Ashen Gate, without proving why the gate changed.
consequence_options: The guild must decide whether a formal re-survey is warranted.
Greyfen gains a concrete reason to watch the old boundary.

eligible_main_saga_milestones.summary: Leyra notices an old private field mark associated with Master Ilyan near the exterior survey stones.
eligible_main_saga_milestones.state_condition: The mark establishes only that Ilyan surveyed or marked this site before; it does not establish why or what he knew.
consequence_options: Leyra's trust question becomes more immediate.

eligible_main_saga_milestones.summary: A second survey condition confirms the gate response is not a single accidental compass twitch.
eligible_main_saga_milestones.state_condition: Leyra has corroborating field evidence that the boundary response is real, while cause remains unresolved.
consequence_options: Master Ilyan can no longer dismiss the event as one bad reading.

creation_constraints: Magic must follow rule-bound cartographic and boundary logic.
New durable facts must not explain why Ashen Gate reopened before the relevant reveal becomes eligible.
New NPCs should have plausible links to guild or border life.
forbidden_creations: Arbitrary spellcasting that bypasses surveying and evidence
Early confirmation of the Nameless Vale's purpose
Predetermined proof that Master Ilyan acted maliciously

architect_raw_payload.title: The Road the Map Refused to Admit
architect_raw_payload.story_promise: Leyra tests an impossible gate response with disciplined method and decides what an honest record can claim.
architect_raw_payload.protagonist_role: Eighteen-year-old junior boundary cartographer preparing for an independent map-seal license.
architect_raw_payload.immediate_objective: Establish what Ashen Gate is doing before dusk and decide what she can responsibly report.
architect_raw_payload.central_question: Is the gate response a real boundary change, or residue and instrument error?
architect_raw_payload.stakes: A false claim could endanger travelers and end her apprenticeship; ignoring a real change leaves Greyfen relying on a wrong map.
constraints: No crossing the sealed boundary without authorization.
The private mark shows prior presence only, not motive or cause.
One session cannot prove why the road returned, what lies in the Nameless Vale, or whether other roads are changing.
Every durable claim must separate witnessed response from theory.
architect_raw_payload.opening_hook: At Ashen Gate, Leyra's ward-compass swings toward a sealed arch and points along a road the legal map says does not exist.

logistics_plan.time_window: Roughly three hours of usable light and ward-response, from mid-afternoon to dusk.
movement_constraints: Vellum Hall to Greyfen is a short morning ride, completed before the window opens.
Greyfen to Ashen Gate is a short ride along the eastern ward-line.
No return travel occurs before the ending; the Vellum Hall report is made by sealed message or a scene set after dusk.
All survey work stays at the exterior markers.
logistics_plan.feasibility_rationale: The hall briefing and Greyfen stop happen in the morning. Leyra reaches Ashen Gate with about three hours left and stays there, so no trip fits inside the shrinking window.

beats.purpose: Set the routine re-survey, Leyra's license review and Ilyan's evasiveness.
beats.character_action: Collects instruments and a bounded re-survey order; Ilyan tells her to log only what she witnesses.
beats.external_event: Ilyan deflects a question about his earlier Ashen Gate work.
beats.new_information: The assignment is routine; outer wardstones have been hard to reconcile with legal maps.
beats.escalation_delta: Baseline: the rule is to record only witnessed facts.
beats.state_change: Leyra carries a procedural standard and an unspoken trust question.
beats.payoff_contribution: Establishes the honesty standard the final record is judged by.

beats.purpose: Show the community cost of a wrong map.
beats.character_action: Stops to confirm livestock-route boundaries and hears the wardens' request for certainty.
beats.external_event: A warden says Greyfen will move animals near the old boundary within days unless told otherwise.
beats.new_information: Greyfen will act on whatever wording Leyra reports.
beats.escalation_delta: Time pressure becomes social: silence and overstatement both have consequences.
beats.state_change: Leyra now owes Greyfen a careful answer.

beats.character_action: Takes a baseline compass reading at the first exterior stone and notes the time, light and tide-independent setup.
beats.external_event: The compass swings toward a continuing line through the sealed arch; the exterior stone warms faintly in answer.
beats.new_information: Reading 1: the needle points along a route the legal map omits.
beats.escalation_delta: The routine survey becomes a possible boundary anomaly.
beats.state_change: Leyra has an unverified single response.
beats.payoff_contribution: The first entry in the dated record.

beats.purpose: Test the easy explanation of residue or a faulty compass.
beats.character_action: Recalibrates on a known stable stone, then repeats the reading from the same spot and again from a second stone using the same compass.
beats.external_event: The calibration stone reads true; both gate readings repeat the swing.
beats.new_information: Three gate readings agree on bearing within a small margin. The compass is sound on a known line.
beats.escalation_delta: The instrument-fault explanation weakens but is not eliminated.
beats.state_change: The response is likely not a single twitch, though the same compass was used throughout.

beats.purpose: Introduce Ilyan's mark without over-explaining it.
beats.character_action: Finds and sketches a weathered private field mark on the lower face of an exterior stone.
beats.external_event: Lichen and wear show the mark is old; its style matches Ilyan's known glyphs.
beats.new_information: OBSERVED: the mark is old and resembles Ilyan's private notation, so he was likely present. Nothing shows why.
beats.escalation_delta: Personal stakes rise: the anomaly may have been known to her mentor.
beats.state_change: Leyra must keep the trust question separate from the evidence.
beats.payoff_contribution: Forces her to record what the mark cannot prove.

beats.purpose: Constrain time and force a strategy change.
beats.character_action: Notices the response weakening as the light lowers and rewrites her plan with the remaining time.
beats.external_event: The needle deflection shrinks over successive checks as the light drops.
beats.new_information: Readings at roughly equal intervals show a progressively weaker deflection: strong, moderate, faint.
beats.escalation_delta: Access to the phenomenon is running out.
beats.state_change: She can no longer do everything and must choose what to prioritise.

beats.purpose: Reinterpret the response as neither residue nor a fixed feature.
beats.character_action: Resets on a fresh stake line with a new chain-measured baseline and takes a further reading.
beats.external_event: The reset reading still points along the omitted route, but its strength matches the fading trend.
beats.new_information: The response survives one independent reset and varies in strength with the fading light or ward conditions.
beats.escalation_delta: The problem changes from whether it is real to what its variable strength means for a claim.
beats.state_change: Her belief that a fixed static residue explains the response is replaced by a condition-dependent response of unknown cause.

beats.character_action: Weighs using the last usable minutes on a reproduction attempt versus preserving a bounded report and dealing with the mark.
beats.external_event: Dusk approaches and the response is near its faintest.
beats.new_information: She cannot do both fully: more testing spends the light the report needs.
beats.escalation_delta: The choice now carries irreversible costs.
beats.payoff_contribution: Determines which durable state is available.

beats.purpose: Dramatize the chosen branch with its fixed result.
beats.character_action: Executes the chosen branch using her existing readings, constraints and method.
beats.external_event: The branch-specific test or presentation occurs as defined in the decision point.
beats.new_information: The branch outcome resolves the local uncertainty as fixed by the decision point.
beats.escalation_delta: Final pressure of fading light and accountability.
beats.state_change: The record is completed or not, per branch.

beats.purpose: Resolve what goes on record and shift trust with Ilyan and Greyfen.
beats.character_action: Delivers the wording and receives Ilyan's verdict as defined by the branch.
beats.external_event: Ilyan and the Greyfen wardens respond to the record's wording.
beats.new_information: What is recorded is bounded; cause, scope, the Nameless Vale and Ilyan's motive stay open.
beats.state_change: Leyra's standing and Greyfen's plans change according to the branch.

beats.character_action: Files the sketch of Ilyan's mark alongside the report and holds back the question she still wants to ask him.
beats.external_event: Ilyan looks at the sketch and says only that the site should not be crossed unwarranted.
beats.new_information: He acknowledges the mark is his but gives no motive.
beats.escalation_delta: A new question replaces the solved one.
beats.state_change: The trust question is now explicit.
beats.payoff_contribution: Forward pull without undoing the payoff.

escalation_ladder: The single compass swing repeats but the instrument-fault explanation is only weakened, not removed.
Ilyan's old mark makes the anomaly personal and possibly previously known.
The response weakens with dusk, forcing a choice about how to spend the remaining time.
The fresh-setup reading shows the response persists but varies, undermining the fixed-residue view and complicating any wording.

reversal.prior_belief: The response is either a one-off compass glitch or a fixed static residue in the stones.

evidence.claim: A calibration stone read true and three gate readings from two stones agreed on bearing with the same compass.
Three readings at roughly equal intervals showed deflection strong, moderate, faint as light dropped, with the setup unchanged.
An old mark resembling Ilyan's notation is on an exterior stone.
The response is unlikely to be a single twitch or purely a fault of the compass on the original setup.
Strength may depend on light or ward conditions rather than being fixed.

reversal.reinterpretation: The gate answers to an omitted route in a condition-dependent way: it is real enough to record as a bounded observation, not a permanent feature.
reversal.inference_ceiling: One fresh-setup repeat shows the reading survives one independent reset. It does not prove setup-independence, rule out all instrument error, show the gate is the cause, or establish recurrence on other days. The fading trend is one afternoon's series with light as an uncontrolled confound; no tide claim is made. The mark shows Ilyan's presence, not motive.
reversal.unresolved_after_reversal: The cause of the response, whether it recurs on other days, what lies beyond the gate, and what Ilyan witnessed.

decision_point.pressure: Little light remains: more reproduction attempts spend the window the report needs, while a bounded report leaves the mark question and reproduction unresolved.

branches.option: Spend the remaining light on another independent reproduction.
branches.immediate_action: Rebuilds a third baseline with new stakes and a different stone pairing, taking timed readings until the response fades.
branches.evidence_state_after_choice: Stronger evidence of a repeatable response under changing light, but the written record is unfinished.
branches.cost_or_risk: The report and mark sketch are rushed, and the wording may be judged incomplete.
branches.relationship_or_access_effect: Ilyan respects the method but faults the unfinished record; Greyfen gets no wording that night.
branches.climax_requirement: Dramatize the last timed reading pair: the deflection is present in the first and gone in the second, the same direction as before, with no crossing.
branches.local_payoff_if_earned: Stronger evidence but no reviewed log: Ilyan orders a proper write-up and follow-up, and forbidden_passage_observed stays pending.

branches.option: Stop testing and write a dated, worded field record while the response is still faintly visible.
branches.immediate_action: Records all readings, setup notes and the sketch of the mark, then sends a bounded notice to Greyfen and Vellum Hall.
branches.evidence_state_after_choice: Complete record of the existing readings, including the fresh-setup reset, but no further reproduction.
branches.cost_or_risk: No extra corroboration; a reviewer may call the sample thin.
branches.relationship_or_access_effect: Ilyan reviews it and Greyfen receives careful wording; the mark question is put to him directly.
branches.climax_requirement: Dramatize the presentation to Ilyan: Leyra separates witnessed response, inference and theory line by line and defends each limit.
branches.local_payoff_if_earned: Ilyan accepts a provisional reviewed log of one bounded anomaly, with cause and scope stated as unknown.

decision_point.what_is_unknown: Which branch Leyra chooses, and whether her reasoning and execution earn it.

architect_raw_payload.climax: Leyra works the chosen branch under failing light using only established readings, the reset baseline and her constraints, without crossing the boundary or adding unplanned evidence.
architect_raw_payload.local_payoff: All branches resolve whether the gate response is real enough to record as a bounded observation, and what may honestly be claimed now. The durable record differs: reproduction gives stronger evidence but no reviewed log, while the bounded report gives a provisional reviewed log. Cause, scope, the Nameless Vale and Ilyan's motive stay open.
architect_raw_payload.forward_hook: Ilyan admits the mark is his, yet Leyra still does not know what he saw or why he left it.

persistent_outcome_candidates.description: A dated, bounded record of the Ashen Gate response to an omitted route.
persistent_outcome_candidates.commit_condition: Only if the prose shows the readings, the reset and the witnessed/inferred/theory separation.

persistent_outcome_candidates.description: Ilyan's trust in Leyra shifts based on how she handled incomplete evidence.
persistent_outcome_candidates.commit_condition: Only if the branch scene shows his reaction.

persistent_outcome_candidates.description: A warranted follow-up survey becomes possible without declaring the passage safe.
persistent_outcome_candidates.commit_condition: Only if the reviewed log is earned, in the bounded branch.

persistent_outcome_candidates.description: Greyfen gains a carefully worded reason to monitor the old boundary.
persistent_outcome_candidates.commit_condition: Only if a bounded notice is delivered.

completion_evidence: A dated field record of a repeated gate response, including at least one fresh-setup reset.
The record separates witnessed response from theory and claims no cause.
In the reproduction branch the milestone is not committed, as no reviewed record is completed.

anti_repetition_signature.core_problem_shape: Separating a real anomaly from artifact under honesty constraints
anti_repetition_signature.main_location_pattern: Hall briefing, village stop, single-site fieldwork
anti_repetition_signature.climax_shape: Branch-specific final reading or defended record under failing light
anti_repetition_signature.distinct_from_recent_episodes_because: No recent episodes exist; the climax is an evidentiary act, not a chase or crossing.

writer_rules: Do not cross the sealed boundary.
Do not explain why the gate responds or reveal Ilyan's motive or the Nameless Vale.
Do not claim a tide correlation; only the light-linked series is observed.
No unplanned new evidence in the climax; only the fixed branch test is allowed.
Do not choose the branch in advance; dramatize the decision, then the fixed branch result.
Do not state a reviewed log exists in the reproduction branch.
Keep the wonder grounded in measurement and exact wording.
